characters.description: The gruff, club-wielding satyr who chaperones the young demigods aboard the Argo II. Quick to threaten and quicker to fight, he guards his charges fiercely beneath the bluster and keeps a rough order on the ship as the dangers mount.
characters.name: Gleeson Hedge

characters.description: The primordial earth goddess, still stirring toward full wakefulness. Speaking through the ground and through dreams, she drives her giants and monsters against the demigods and schemes to keep the Doors of Death open so her forces cannot be stopped, edging ever closer to the moment she can rise and remake the world.
characters.name: Gaea

recaps.ending: Both journeys converge on the House of Hades in the Greek region of Epirus. In Tartarus, Percy and Annabeth reach the Doors of Death with the help of the kindly Titan Bob and the giant Damasen, who give their lives so the two demigods can pass through, and the couple emerges battered but alive on the mortal side. There the rest of the crew has fought its way to the same place, and together they seal the Doors of Death, cutting off Gaea's endless supply of revived monsters. Along the way the heroes have grown stronger and closer: Hazel has mastered a magic of illusion, Frank has come into his full power, and Leo, briefly cast away on the hidden island of Ogygia, has fallen in love with the immortal Calypso and sworn to return and free her. With the Doors closed and all seven reunited, the crew turns toward Athens, where Gaea intends to wake fully and where the giants plan to make their final stand. To keep the Greek and Roman camps from destroying each other in the meantime, Nico di Angelo, the Roman leader Reyna, and Coach Hedge take on the dangerous task of carrying the Athena Parthenos statue across the world to Camp Half-Blood as a token of peace. The book ends with the two efforts underway: the ship racing to Athens for the reckoning with Gaea, and the statue's bearers setting out to prevent a war between the camps.
recaps.in_short: The story follows two paths. Below, Percy and Annabeth struggle across Tartarus toward the underside of the Doors of Death, surviving on nerve and each other, and are aided by a gentle, memory-clouded Titan named Bob and a lonely giant, Damasen. Above, the crew of the Argo II, Jason, Piper, Leo, Hazel, Frank, Nico, and Coach Hedge, sails to the House of Hades in Greece to close the Doors from the mortal side so their friends can escape and Gaea's forces can be shut out. Along the way each hero grows: Hazel learns to bend the mist and work magic, Frank comes fully into his strength, Leo is stranded on a hidden island and meets and falls for the sorceress Calypso, and Nico wrestles with secrets of his own. The two groups fight through to the Doors at the same moment; with sacrifices from their underworld allies, Percy and Annabeth escape Tartarus and the Doors are sealed. All seven are reunited, but Gaea's rising nears its climax, and Nico, Reyna, and Coach Hedge set out on a separate mission to carry the Athena Parthenos statue home and stop a war between the Greek and Roman camps.

recaps.text: Previously: Seven demigods, Greek and Roman, were prophesied to stop the primordial earth goddess Gaea, who is waking and raising the giants. After the goddess Hera swapped heroes to force the two long-separated camps together, the Greek hero Percy Jackson, son of the sea god, and the Roman newcomers Hazel and Frank joined the sky god's son Jason and the new demigods Piper and Leo. Aboard the flying warship Argo II they sailed for the ancient lands to close the Doors of Death, the passage that lets Gaea's slain monsters return. Reaching Rome, Annabeth, daughter of Athena, recovered a lost statue meant to reconcile the camps, but in the process she and Percy fell together into Tartarus, the abyss beneath the underworld. As this book opens, the couple is trapped below, trying to reach the underside of the Doors, while their friends sail on toward the House of Hades in Greece to close the Doors from the mortal side and bring them home.

characters.description: A woman in her twenties who has been living out of her car since her release from prison, applying for any job that will take someone with a conviction on her record. She is practical, observant, and used to being turned down once an employer runs a background check, so she says as little about her past as she can get away with. Offered a live-in housekeeping position with a wealthy family, she takes it knowing she has no better option.
characters.name: Millie Calloway

characters.description: The woman of the Winchester house, a wealthy Long Island wife who conducts Millie's interview with warmth and no real scrutiny and hires her on the spot. She is disorganized, effusive, and hard to read, and her attention moves quickly from one thing to another.
characters.name: Nina Winchester

characters.description: Nina's husband, a handsome and successful man who is unfailingly courteous to the staff and easy to talk to. He apologizes for his wife's behaviour where others would complain about it, and he is the only person in the house who treats Millie as a person rather than as hired help.
characters.name: Andrew Winchester

characters.description: The Winchesters' nine-year-old daughter, devoted to ballet and impeccably behaved. She is polite to Millie in a way that never becomes friendly, watches more than she says, and seems entirely untroubled by what happens between her parents.
characters.name: Cecelia Winchester

characters.description: The Italian landscaper who maintains the Winchesters' grounds. He speaks little English and Millie speaks no Italian, but he goes out of his way to make her understand that she is in danger and should leave the house, which she cannot afford to do.
characters.name: Enzo Accardi

characters.description: Andrew's mother, immaculate, imposing, and entirely certain of her place. She keeps her son's household at arm's length and makes clear that the Winchester name and the Winchester money are hers to look after.
characters.name: Evelyn Winchester

characters.description: A woman who was engaged to Andrew Winchester years before he married Nina. The engagement ended abruptly and nobody who knew her has heard from her since.
characters.name: Kathleen Connelly

recaps.ending: Locked in the attic and left without food or water, Millie gets the door open, and when Andrew comes for her she puts him in the room instead and turns the lock. She keeps him there. He goes through the same starvation and confinement he inflicted on Nina and on Kathleen Connelly before her, and he does not come out alive. Enzo, who tried to warn Millie from the beginning, helps her deal with what is left. Evelyn Winchester makes it clear that she has known for years what her son was and has spent those years managing it, and Andrew's death is never treated as a crime by anyone with the power to treat it as one. Nina and Cecelia are free of him and safe, with the Winchester money behind them. Millie leaves the house with her record intact but her life her own, in a relationship with Enzo and no longer sleeping in her car. The closing pages put her back at work in another wealthy household, watching another family, with the clear implication that what she learned in that attic is something she now intends to use.
recaps.in_short: Millie Calloway, recently out of prison and living in her car, is hired as the live-in housekeeper for the Winchesters in a wealthy Long Island suburb. Her room is a stifling attic with a lock fitted to the outside of the door. Nina Winchester is erratic and cruel, creating messes and accusations Millie cannot answer, while Andrew Winchester is patient, charming and sympathetic, and Millie ends up in bed with him. When Nina finally leaves and takes their daughter, everything Millie believed turns out to be inverted: Andrew is a sadist who punished his wife by locking her in that attic without food or water, who destroyed her credibility so that nobody would believe her, and who had done the same to a woman before her. Nina hired Millie, a woman convicted of killing someone, and made herself unbearable on purpose. Locked in the attic in her turn, Millie gets out, traps Andrew inside it, and leaves him there to die. Andrew's mother ensures nothing comes of it, and Millie walks away free.

recaps.text: The book opens with a brief glimpse of a house full of police and a body upstairs, then goes back to how it started. Millie Calloway, in her twenties and living out of her car with a prison record she leaves off every application, interviews for a live-in housekeeping job at the Winchester house in a wealthy Long Island suburb. Nina Winchester is friendly, scattered and barely interested in her references, and hires her on the spot, which Millie knows is more luck than she has any right to expect. The salary is generous and the room is included. The room turns out to be in the attic: small, airless, with a window that does not open and a lock fitted to the outside of the door. Millie takes the job anyway. Nina's husband Andrew is courteous and easy company, and their nine-year-old daughter Cecelia is polite in a way that does not resemble warmth.

Once Millie has moved in, Nina turns. The instructions she gives contradict the ones she gave the day before, the house is wrecked as fast as Millie can clean it, and Millie is accused of losing things that were never lost and of taking things she never touched. Nina's moods swing without warning between effusive friendliness and cold accusation, and there is no version of the work that counts as done. Andrew apologizes for his wife, quietly and repeatedly, and asks Millie to be patient with her. Enzo, the Italian landscaper, stops Millie in the garden and makes her understand, with the few words they share, that the house is dangerous and she should leave it. Millie has nowhere else to go, a record that closes every other door, and a job that pays. She stays.

The accusations sharpen into something that looks deliberate. Things Millie is supposed to have stolen appear in her attic room, appointments she was never told about are held against her, and Nina begins to build a case against her in front of witnesses. Cecelia contributes, calmly and without any apparent motive. Millie starts to suspect she is being set up for a dismissal that would also send her back to prison, and she has no way to prove any of it. Andrew tells her something of the marriage: that Nina has been ill, that she spent time in a psychiatric facility, and that he has arranged his life around keeping her stable and keeping their daughter's world intact. Millie believes him. Nothing she has seen of Nina contradicts it.

Nina is away from the house more and more, and when she is in it her behaviour is worse. Andrew absorbs all of it without complaint and keeps apologizing to the woman his wife is mistreating, and Millie's sympathy for him hardens into something else. The two of them are alone together more often than not, and the distance between employer and employee stops meaning very much. Millie has spent ten years learning what people are capable of, and everything she has seen in this house tells her the same thing: the cruelty here belongs to Nina, and Andrew is the person trapped with it. She also knows that if Nina decides to accuse her of something serious, a woman with her record will not be given the benefit of any doubt.

Millie and Andrew begin an affair. Millie tells herself she is not taking anything from a marriage that has been over for years, and Andrew describes a life spent managing a woman who cannot be reasoned with. Nina's behaviour becomes more erratic and more public, and the household is openly split: Millie and Andrew on one side, Nina and Cecelia on the other. Millie is now certain that she understands the Winchesters, that Nina is unstable and dangerous and that Andrew is the person trapped with her. Enzo's warning still stands, and Millie has stopped listening to it.

Everything Millie believed is inverted. Nina was never the danger in the house. Andrew is a sadist who punished his wife for trivial infractions by locking her in the attic room for days without food or water, escalating over years of marriage, and who methodically destroyed her credibility so that nobody who heard her would believe her. The psychiatric hospitalization was his doing. She stayed because leaving without her daughter was unthinkable and because she had no proof of anything, and she learned that a woman had been engaged to Andrew before her, Kathleen Connelly, who broke it off and was never heard from again. Nina hired Millie deliberately, knowing she had served ten years for killing a man who was attacking another girl, and then made herself impossible to work for so that Millie would turn to Andrew. Then she filed for divorce and left the house with Cecelia, leaving Millie behind in it.

With Nina gone, Andrew's patience disappears. The charm Millie fell for is replaced by a set of rules, and the first time she breaks one he puts her in the attic and locks the door from the outside. He leaves her there in the heat without food or water, comes back only to explain what she did wrong, and makes clear how long she will stay. Millie understands what the room is for and what happened in it to Nina, and what most likely happened to the woman before Nina. Nobody is coming: the house is isolated, her employer controls every account of her, and a woman with her record who accuses a man like Andrew Winchester will not be believed. She has to get herself out.

Millie gets the attic door open, and when Andrew comes back for her she puts him inside it and locks it. She leaves him there through the same deprivation he used on his wife, and he dies in the room he built for other people. Enzo helps her handle what follows. Evelyn Winchester arrives and makes it clear that she has known for years what her son was and has spent those years cleaning up after him, and Andrew's death is never treated as a crime. Nina and Cecelia are safe and free of him, with the family money behind them. Millie leaves the house with her record unchanged and her life her own, together with Enzo. The book closes with her taking work in another wealthy household, watching another family closely, having decided what she is willing to do about the kind of man she found in that attic.

characters.description: A sixteen-year-old girl from the Seam, the poorest quarter of District 12, the coal-mining district of the nation of Panem. Since her father died in a mine explosion she has kept her mother and younger sister alive by hunting illegally in the woods beyond the fence with a bow, trading her kills at the black market. Guarded, self-reliant, and quick to distrust the Capitol that rules the districts, she volunteers to take her sister's place when the girl is chosen for the Hunger Games. She is a practical survivor rather than a natural performer, uneasy with the cameras and public roles the Games force on her.
characters.name: Katniss Everdeen

characters.description: The son of District 12's baker, chosen as the male tribute alongside Katniss. Sturdy and strong from hauling flour, he is also warm, well-spoken, and good at charming a crowd. Years earlier, when Katniss and her family were starving, he deliberately burned two loaves of bread so he could give them to her, a kindness she has never forgotten. He decorates the bakery's cakes and has a painter's eye that later proves useful.
characters.name: Peeta Mellark

characters.description: Katniss's gentle younger sister, twelve years old, whose name is drawn at the reaping. She loves animals, keeps a scruffy tomcat and a goat, and is learning healing from their mother. She is the person Katniss loves most and the reason Katniss volunteers for the Games.
characters.name: Primrose Everdeen

characters.description: Katniss's closest friend and hunting partner, an eighteen-year-old from the Seam who also supports a fatherless family. Skilled with snares and openly resentful of the Capitol, he shares Katniss's illegal trips into the woods and her anger at the district's poverty.
characters.name: Gale Hawthorne

characters.description: District 12's only living victor of the Hunger Games and therefore the mentor assigned to guide Katniss and Peeta. He is almost always drunk and appears at the reaping in a stupor, but beneath the wreckage he is shrewd about how the Games and their Capitol audience really work.
characters.name: Haymitch Abernathy

characters.description: The Capitol escort for District 12's tributes, with elaborate wigs, bright costumes, and fussy, cheerful manners. She conducts the reaping, drawing the names, and is obsessed with schedules, etiquette, and making a good impression in the Capitol, largely oblivious to the horror of what she is arranging.
characters.name: Effie Trinket

characters.description: Katniss's stylist for the Games, notably understated for a Capitol resident. Rather than making her merely pretty, he dresses her in costumes evoking flame, presenting her as the girl on fire and helping the audience remember her. Calm and quietly sympathetic, he becomes one of the few Capitol figures Katniss trusts.
characters.name: Cinna

characters.description: The twelve-year-old girl tribute from District 11, small, light, and easy to overlook, who reminds Katniss painfully of her sister Prim. Katniss first notices her during the training days, where Rue proves nimble and knowledgeable about plants and moves through high places with ease.
characters.name: Rue

characters.description: A large, aggressive tribute from District 2 and the dominant member of the Career pack, the tributes from wealthier districts who train for the Games and treat them as an honor. Ruthless and physically powerful, he is an early favorite to win and leads the hunt for the other tributes.
characters.name: Cato

characters.description: A tribute from District 2 and a member of the Career pack, deadly with thrown knives. She corners Katniss at the feast, taunting her before trying to kill her.
characters.name: Clove

characters.description: The powerful male tribute from District 11, large and strong, who keeps to himself throughout the Games. He shares a district with Rue, a fact that shapes a decisive choice he makes toward Katniss at the feast.
characters.name: Thresh

characters.description: The president of Panem and head of the Capitol, who presides over the ceremony crowning the victors. Composed and coldly controlled, he embodies the regime whose authority Katniss's actions in the arena have quietly challenged.
characters.name: President Snow

recaps.ending: Katniss and Peeta are the last tributes alive when the Gamemakers revoke the rule that would have let a district's pair win together, ordering them to fight to a single victor. Katniss instead proposes that they both eat poisonous nightlock berries, denying the Games any winner. Before they can, the Capitol relents and declares them joint victors, and both survive to be crowned. Afterward, Haymitch warns Katniss that her gesture was read as an act of rebellion and that the authorities, led by President Snow, are furious with her. Peeta is wounded to learn that some of her tenderness in the arena was a performance for the cameras and sponsors, leaving their relationship unresolved. They ride the train home to District 12 as celebrated champions, but Katniss now stands as an accidental symbol of defiance against the Capitol, a position that marks her as a target and sets up the wider unrest of the books that follow.
recaps.in_short: In the nation of Panem, the wealthy Capitol keeps its twelve districts obedient with the annual Hunger Games, a televised fight to the death between children chosen by lottery. When her twelve-year-old sister is drawn, sixteen-year-old Katniss Everdeen of impoverished District 12 volunteers to take her place and is sent to the arena alongside Peeta Mellark, the baker's son who once helped her survive. Coached by their drunken mentor Haymitch and made memorable by her stylist Cinna, Katniss becomes a public favorite. In the arena she survives the opening slaughter, allies with a small girl named Rue whose death hardens her against the Capitol, and reunites with a wounded Peeta after a rule change allows two tributes from one district to win together. The pair play up a romance to win sponsors and outlast their rivals. When the rule is reversed and only one may live, they threaten to poison themselves together, forcing the Capitol to crown them both. Katniss returns home a victor, but her defiance has made her an enemy of the ruling Capitol.

recaps.text: In the poor coal-mining District 12 of Panem, sixteen-year-old Katniss Everdeen hunts illegally in the woods to feed her mother and younger sister, Prim, after her father's death in a mine accident. The ruling Capitol forces each of its twelve districts to send one boy and one girl each year to the Hunger Games, a televised fight to the death, as punishment for a long-ago rebellion. At the reaping ceremony, run by the Capitol escort Effie Trinket, Prim's name is drawn, and Katniss immediately volunteers to take her place. The boy chosen is Peeta Mellark, the baker's son, who once secretly gave Katniss bread when her family was starving. Watched over by their perpetually drunk mentor Haymitch, the district's only living victor, Katniss says her goodbyes to Prim, her mother, and her hunting partner Gale, and is given a small mockingjay pin as a token from home before she is taken away to the Capitol.

Katniss and Peeta travel to the gleaming Capitol, where Katniss's stylist Cinna dresses her in flames for the opening ceremony, making her the memorable girl on fire. During several days of training with the other tributes, she sizes up her rivals, including the deadly, well-fed Career tributes who treat the Games as an honor and a tiny twelve-year-old from District 11 named Rue. In her private session before the Gamemakers she shoots an arrow near them to force their attention and earns a surprisingly high score. Haymitch coaches the pair to appear as a team. In the televised interviews, Peeta stuns everyone by confessing on air that he has long been in love with Katniss, casting them as doomed sweethearts, a story she cannot tell is genuine or a survival strategy Haymitch has approved.

The tributes are lifted into an outdoor arena, and Katniss avoids the bloodbath at the central Cornucopia, fleeing into the woods and relying on her hunting skills to find water and stay hidden. Several tributes die in the opening minutes. The Career pack, now traveling with Peeta, hunts Katniss and traps her up a tall tree. Rue, hiding in a nearby tree, silently points out a nest of venomous tracker jacker wasps hanging above the sleeping Careers. Katniss saws the nest loose so it drops onto them, killing one and scattering the rest, and she seizes a fallen bow and arrows. Badly stung and hallucinating from the venom, she stumbles away and is quietly tended by Rue until she recovers.

Katniss and Rue form an alliance, sharing food and knowledge. They plan to cripple the Careers by destroying the supplies the pack has hoarded near the Cornucopia; Katniss triggers the buried mines protecting the pile and blows it up, cutting off the Careers' food. Returning to find Rue, she arrives just as another tribute spears the girl. Katniss kills him, then stays with Rue as she dies, singing to her and covering her body with wildflowers, a quiet gesture of defiance meant to shame the Capitol on camera. In gratitude for what she did for their tribute, the people of District 11 send Katniss a gift of bread. Grieving and newly determined, Katniss is left more openly opposed to the Games than ever.

The Gamemakers announce a change: two tributes from the same district may now win together, and Katniss sets out to find Peeta. She discovers him gravely wounded and camouflaged beside a stream, his leg infected, and hides them both in a cave. To win gifts from sponsors she plays up their romance, and her displays of affection earn small parcels of aid. When a feast is announced offering each tribute something they desperately need, Katniss goes to retrieve medicine for Peeta despite the danger. There Clove of District 2 pins her down and taunts her, but Thresh of District 11 kills Clove and spares Katniss because of her kindness to Rue. Katniss brings the medicine back and heals Peeta as their numbers dwindle.

With Peeta recovering, the remaining tributes are drawn together. Foxface, the cunning girl from District 5, dies after eating poisonous nightlock berries that Peeta had gathered without knowing what they were. The Gamemakers unleash monstrous creatures to force a final confrontation at the Cornucopia with Cato, who is eventually killed, leaving Katniss and Peeta as the last two alive. The Gamemakers then revoke the rule allowing two victors, demanding that only one survive. Rather than kill each other, Katniss and Peeta threaten to eat the deadly nightlock together, denying the Capitol any winner; the Gamemakers relent and declare them both victors. Crowned as champions, Katniss learns from Haymitch that her defiant stunt has embarrassed and angered the Capitol and its president, Snow. Peeta is hurt to realize her arena romance was partly an act, and the two return home united in name but uncertain with each other, and dangerously out of favor with the regime.

characters.description: The veteran Soviet submarine captain chosen to command Red October, a new ballistic-missile submarine equipped with an unusually quiet propulsion system. A Lithuanian by birth and the son of a fisherman, he is respected as a demanding teacher of other captains and has selected senior officers he trusts for the boat's first voyage.
characters.name: Marko Ramius

characters.description: Red October's political officer, responsible for representing Party authority aboard the submarine. His presence gives him power outside the normal naval chain of command and makes him the officer most able to challenge Ramius's control of the voyage.
characters.name: Ivan Putin

characters.description: The executive officer of Red October and Ramius's closest professional confidant aboard the submarine. He helps manage the crew and shares the captain's confidence concerning the officers' private purpose for the voyage.
characters.name: Vasily Borodin

characters.description: The medical officer aboard Red October. He is outside Ramius's small circle of co-conspirators and must judge the captain's explanations from the evidence available to an ordinary member of the crew.
characters.name: Yevgeny Petrov

characters.description: A former Marine officer, historian, and occasional CIA analyst working in Britain. He has an unusual ability to connect military detail with personal motive, and his access to intelligence about Soviet naval officers draws him into the international response to Red October's disappearance.
characters.name: Jack Ryan

characters.description: The CIA's deputy director for intelligence and Ryan's senior sponsor. Greer values Ryan's independent judgment and brings him into the urgent effort to understand why the Soviet fleet has suddenly put to sea.
characters.name: James Greer

characters.description: The commanding officer of the American attack submarine USS Dallas. Patient and tactically alert, he gives his sonar team room to pursue an uncertain contact that standard equipment initially fails to classify.
characters.name: Bart Mancuso

characters.description: A sonar operator aboard USS Dallas with an exceptional ear for patterns hidden in underwater noise. He treats acoustic analysis as a practical science and suspects that a faint, rhythmic disturbance dismissed by the computer may be a submarine using unfamiliar machinery.
characters.name: Ronald Jones

characters.description: The United States national security adviser, coordinating the White House response to the Soviet naval emergency. He must weigh Ryan's interpretation against the danger that Red October could be approaching the American coast as a first-strike weapon.
characters.name: Jeffrey Pelt

characters.description: A skilled Soviet attack-submarine captain who once trained under Ramius. Commanding the fast Alfa-class V. K. Konovalov, he joins the broad search for Red October and knows enough of his former teacher's habits to be a particularly dangerous pursuer.
characters.name: Viktor Tupolev

characters.description: A naval systems expert at the United States Naval Academy and an old colleague of Ryan's. His analysis of reconnaissance photographs helps explain the scale and military purpose of Red October's novel propulsion arrangement.
characters.name: Skip Tyler

characters.description: Red October's chief engineer, responsible for the nuclear plant and the new caterpillar propulsion system. His technical knowledge is essential to keeping the submarine operational during a voyage whose true demands are known only to its officers.
characters.name: Alexander Melekhin

recaps.ending: After Red October's enlisted crew is removed and returned to Soviet custody under the cover of a reactor emergency, a small American party joins Ramius and his officers aboard the submarine. A concealed Soviet intelligence officer remains behind, kills Vasily Borodin, wounds Ramius, and attempts to destroy the ship before Ryan stops him. The Americans continue the deception by sinking the obsolete USS Ethan Allen where Soviet observers can mistake it for Red October. Tupolev nevertheless finds the real submarine in the Atlantic and attacks in V. K. Konovalov. In the final underwater engagement, Ramius uses Red October itself to ram and sink the Soviet attack submarine, eliminating the last immediate witness to the defection. Red October survives and is secretly taken into American possession for study. Ramius and the surviving officers reach the United States, while Ryan returns home exhausted after helping deliver both the defectors and their technologically valuable submarine.
recaps.in_short: Marko Ramius takes the Soviet Union's newest missile submarine, Red October, into the Atlantic with a handpicked group of officers and a plan to defect with the vessel. After his advance letter alerts Moscow, the Soviet fleet races to destroy him while telling the United States that it is conducting a rescue. CIA analyst Jack Ryan concludes that Ramius intends to surrender rather than launch an attack and persuades American leaders to risk making contact. USS Dallas locates the nearly silent submarine, and Ryan boards it after Ramius stages an engineering casualty that removes the enlisted crew. The Americans fake Red October's destruction by sinking an obsolete submarine, but a hidden Soviet agent kills Borodin and nearly sabotages the boat before Ryan stops him. Ramius then defeats the pursuing V. K. Konovalov by ramming it. The defecting officers and Red October reach American control, giving the United States both the men and the Soviet submarine's secret propulsion technology.

recaps.text: The Soviet Union sends Red October, a new ballistic-missile submarine, on its first operational voyage under Captain Marko Ramius. The boat's caterpillar drive can move it with very little of the mechanical noise normally used to track submarines. Shortly after sailing, Ramius kills political officer Ivan Putin and makes the death appear accidental, leaving himself firmly in command. He has also sent a letter to Admiral Padorin whose contents prompt an extraordinary Soviet reaction: much of the Northern Fleet is ordered into the Atlantic to find Red October. The United States detects the mass deployment but cannot tell whether it signals an exercise, a rescue effort, or preparation for war. In London and Washington, CIA analyst Jack Ryan is pulled into the effort to identify the submarine and understand Ramius's intentions.

American intelligence learns that Red October carries long-range missiles and a nearly silent drive, making a hostile approach to the United States a grave threat. The Soviets privately claim that Ramius has gone mad and ask for help sinking his boat, while their own ships and submarines spread across the Atlantic. Ryan studies Ramius's record and personal history rather than accepting the Soviet account. He argues that the captain may be trying to leave the Soviet Union with the submarine, although the evidence remains circumstantial and the consequences of being wrong would be catastrophic. Meanwhile, USS Dallas detects a faint rhythmic disturbance that sonar operator Ronald Jones connects to an unknown vessel. Captain Bart Mancuso follows the contact and begins tracking a submarine that conventional systems can barely hear.

Ryan persuades the American leadership that Ramius's actions fit a defection attempt better than a missile attack. His case depends on the captain's grievances, the officers selected for the voyage, and Red October's route, but no direct communication has confirmed it. The United States develops a plan to approach without letting the Soviet Union learn that its most advanced submarine might be captured. Dallas maintains contact through Jones's acoustic work and maneuvers close enough to test Ramius's response. Carefully exchanged signals show that the Soviet captain is willing to cooperate. Ryan, despite having no experience conducting an operation at sea, is sent forward because he understands the theory behind the mission and can speak directly for the officials who accepted his judgment.

The Americans and Ramius coordinate an elaborate transfer. Ramius creates the appearance of a dangerous reactor casualty and orders Red October's enlisted crew to abandon ship, telling them that the officers will remain behind to scuttle her. The evacuated sailors can therefore be returned to Soviet custody believing that their submarine was lost. Ryan and a small American naval party board Red October, where Ramius and his senior officers openly commit themselves to asylum in the United States. To support the cover story, the Americans prepare the obsolete submarine USS Ethan Allen to be destroyed where Soviet observers can register a convincing underwater loss. The operation has moved from interpreting Ramius's intentions to preserving the submarine and concealing its capture, while Soviet forces continue searching nearby.

Most of Red October's crew is safely off the submarine, and the planned destruction of Ethan Allen supplies evidence for the fiction that Ramius's boat has sunk. One threat remains aboard: a concealed Soviet intelligence operative who stayed behind among the crew. He kills Borodin, wounds Ramius, and tries to sabotage the submarine's missiles and machinery. Ryan pursues and kills him before he can destroy the vessel. The surviving Soviet officers and Americans regain control, but Captain Tupolev in V. K. Konovalov has continued hunting independently and closes on Red October. The defectors now face a Soviet commander who recognizes his former teacher's tactics and can expose the entire deception if he escapes to report what he has found.

V. K. Konovalov attacks Red October, forcing Ramius and the American submariners into a close underwater battle. Rather than allow Tupolev to escape or keep firing, Ramius turns the larger Red October into the Soviet attack submarine and rams it, sinking Konovalov with all hands. Red October remains afloat despite the collision. With the last direct pursuer gone and the false sinking accepted, the Americans guide the captured submarine to safety under strict secrecy. Ramius and his surviving officers complete their defection and enter the United States; Borodin, who had imagined a new life there, is the principal loss among them. The United States gains access to Red October's quiet-drive technology as well as the intelligence carried by her officers. Ryan's deduction has proved correct, and he returns to his family after taking part personally in the dangerous final stages of the operation.

characters.description: A Ranger's apprentice from Redmont, taken prisoner when he and Evanlyn burned the bridge Morgarath's slaves had built. He is aboard a Skandian wolfship heading north as a captive, without weapons, horse or any prospect of rescue, and knows that captured foreigners in Skandia are put to work as slaves. He is resourceful and observant, and he is very young to be as far from home as he now is.
characters.name: Will

characters.description: Will's fellow captive, who has kept up the story that she is a servant of Princess Cassandra. She is in fact Cassandra herself, King Duncan's daughter and the heir to Araluen, which she cannot afford anyone in Skandia to discover. She is practical, stubborn and better at reading people than Will is, and she carries the whole weight of the deception.
characters.name: Evanlyn

characters.description: The Skandian jarl who captured Will and Evanlyn and captains the wolfship carrying them north. He is huge, blunt and profane, a professional raider who regards prisoners as goods rather than enemies, and who is a good deal more decent than his trade suggests. He respects competence, including in people he has taken.
characters.name: Erak

characters.description: Erak's second in command aboard the wolfship, cheerfully loyal to his jarl and untroubled by the ethics of raiding.
characters.name: Svengal

characters.description: The King's Ranger for Redmont Fief, who has just helped win Araluen's war and now wants only one thing: to go after his apprentice. He is not a man who accepts a refusal, and the more politely he is told no, the more dangerous his intentions become.
characters.name: Halt

characters.description: A Battleschool apprentice who killed Morgarath in single combat and is now treated across Araluen as a hero, which embarrasses him. He is loyal to Will and to Halt, literal-minded, and formidable with a sword well beyond his years and rank.
characters.name: Horace Altman

characters.description: The King of Araluen, grateful to Halt and to Will but facing a kingdom to rebuild after the war and a missing daughter whose situation he cannot make public. He needs his Rangers where they are, and he cannot be seen to bend the law for one of them.
characters.name: King Duncan

characters.description: The Oberjarl of Skandia, ruler of the northern raiders from his great hall at Hallasholm. He is violent, quick-tempered and absolute among his own people, and he has sworn a blood oath, the Vallasvow, against the royal family of Araluen, which binds him to kill any of them he finds.
characters.name: Ragnak

characters.description: The Oberjarl's hilfmann, the administrator who runs Hallasholm's accounts, stores and slaves while the warriors raid. He is thin, harassed and entirely unsentimental, and decides which slaves work in the hall and which are sent to the yard.
characters.name: Borsa

characters.description: A warlord in Gallica, the lawless country between Araluen and Skandia, who has carved out a private domain around his black castle, Chateau Montsombre. He is elegant, cultured and cruel, keeps the bodies of those who displease him on display, and collects skilled fighting men. He treats unwanted visitors as guests who may not leave.
characters.name: Deparnieux

recaps.ending: Erak, who has watched what the yard has done to Will, arranges for the two captives to get out of Hallasholm, with supplies and a direction rather than an escort, and covers their disappearance. Evanlyn takes Will up into the mountains to an abandoned hunter's cabin as the Skandian winter closes the country down. Will arrives barely able to function, wanting nothing but the drug, and Evanlyn keeps him there and brings him through the withdrawal herself: days of shaking, sickness and fury, with the two of them snowed in and no help within reach. By the end of the book the worst of it is behind him and he is beginning to think and act like himself again, though he is weak and the two of them are stranded far from any friendly territory with the winter still to survive. Halt and Horace, free of Deparnieux and out of Gallica at last, are moving north towards Skandia to look for him. The two parties have still not met when the book closes, and Evanlyn's identity remains a secret whose exposure in Ragnak's country would be fatal.
recaps.in_short: Will and Evanlyn are carried north to Skandia as captives of the jarl Erak. In Araluen, Halt is refused permission to go after his apprentice, so he deliberately insults King Duncan in public until he is banished for a year, which frees him to leave; Horace goes with him. In Skandia the two prisoners are made slaves in the Oberjarl Ragnak's hall, and Evanlyn must hide that she is Princess Cassandra, because Ragnak has sworn a blood oath against Araluen's royal house. Will is sent to the slave yard and given warmweed, the drug that keeps the labourers docile, and is steadily hollowed out by it. Crossing lawless Gallica, Halt and Horace are trapped as unwilling guests of the warlord Deparnieux; Halt manoeuvres him into a formal challenge and Horace kills him. Erak helps Evanlyn get Will out of Hallasholm before winter, and she takes him to a mountain cabin and forces him through withdrawal, while Halt and Horace push north still searching.

recaps.text: Previously: Will, an orphan ward of Castle Redmont, was apprenticed to the Ranger Halt and trained as one of the King's scouts, and helped destroy the Kalkara that the exiled rebel lord Morgarath sent to murder Araluen's commanders. When Morgarath finally invaded, King Duncan sent the Ranger Gilan into neighbouring Celtica with Will and Will's friend Horace, a Battleschool apprentice, to call in Celtic troops. They found the country emptied and one survivor, a girl called Evanlyn who said she served Princess Cassandra, and discovered that Morgarath's Wargals had enslaved the Celts to build a bridge across the gorge protecting Araluen's flank, so that an army could take the King's forces from behind. Gilan rode back to warn the army; the other three burned the bridge. Horace escaped and reached the army, but Will and Evanlyn were captured by Skandian mercenaries under the jarl Erak and taken away by sea. Halt destroyed the Wargal flanking column, and Horace killed Morgarath in single combat, ending the war. Afterwards it emerged that Evanlyn is really Cassandra, King Duncan's daughter and the heir to Araluen. She and Will are being carried north to Skandia, where captives are worked as slaves, and Halt intends to go after them.

Will and Evanlyn are prisoners aboard Erak's wolfship on a long, punishing voyage north, with storms, cold and a crew who treat them as cargo. Evanlyn holds to her story that she is Princess Cassandra's maid, since a servant is worth a modest ransom or a sale while the heir to Araluen would be worth something far more dangerous. In Araluen, Halt asks King Duncan to release him from duty so that he can go after his apprentice. The King, rebuilding a kingdom after the war and unable to spare a senior Ranger, refuses him. Halt does not argue the point, which anyone who knows him would find ominous.

Halt finds the one route out that the King cannot block. He appears in public and insults Duncan deliberately and repeatedly, in front of witnesses, until the King has no choice under his own law but to banish him from Araluen for a year. It is exactly the outcome Halt wanted, and it costs him his position, his standing and his friendships to get it. Horace, refusing to let him travel alone, contrives to go with him, and the two of them cross to Gallica, the lawless country between Araluen and the northern seas, where central authority has collapsed and self-appointed warlords hold the roads. Will and Evanlyn's voyage continues north.

The wolfship reaches Hallasholm, the Skandian capital, and the two captives are handed over to Borsa, the Oberjarl's administrator, and set to work as slaves in Ragnak's great hall. Evanlyn learns how close to death her secret has brought her: Ragnak, the Oberjarl, has sworn the Vallasvow, a blood oath against the royal family of Araluen, and would be bound to kill her if her name were known. Erak, who captured them, quietly keeps an eye on both. In Gallica, Halt and Horace make slow progress through a country of bandits and petty warlords, where Horace's skill with a sword repeatedly settles matters that talking cannot.

Will is taken out of the hall and sent to the yard, the heavy-labour gang that hauls timber and stores for Hallasholm, where the work is brutal and the slaves are kept compliant with warmweed. The drug takes hold quickly. Within weeks Will is docile, incurious and interested in nothing except his ration, and the boy who trained under Halt is effectively gone. In Gallica, Halt and Horace fall into the hands of Deparnieux, a wealthy and sadistic warlord who takes them to his castle at Montsombre and keeps them there as guests who are not permitted to leave, intrigued by Horace's ability and unwilling to release either of them.

Evanlyn, still working in the hall, sees what has been done to Will and realises he will not survive another season in the yard. She has no allies, no money and no way north or south, and the Skandian winter is closing in, which will shut the country down for months. At Montsombre, Halt plays a long game with Deparnieux, flattering his vanity and studying his household while the weeks pass, aware that every week costs Will something. Neither prisoner can simply be fought free: Deparnieux has a private army, and the two Araluens have to be given a way out that the warlord's own code will not let him refuse.

Erak decides to act. He arranges for Will and Evanlyn to slip out of Hallasholm with supplies and covers their absence, and Evanlyn takes Will up into the mountains to an abandoned hunting cabin before the snow closes the passes. Will is by then barely functional and wants only the drug. In Gallica, Halt manoeuvres Deparnieux into issuing a formal challenge that his own reputation obliges him to honour, and Horace fights and kills him, which frees them both and ends the warlord's hold on the district. With the road finally open, they turn north.

Snowed into the cabin, Evanlyn brings Will through warmweed withdrawal on her own: days of sickness, shaking, rage and pleading, with nowhere to go for help and nothing to do but hold him there until it passes. By the end of the book the worst is over and Will is beginning to come back to himself, though he is weak and both of them are stranded deep in enemy country with the winter still ahead. Halt and Horace, out of Gallica at last, are pressing north to search for him. The two parties have not met when the book closes, and Evanlyn's real identity remains a secret that would be fatal in Ragnak's country.

characters.description: The Alchemist running the Palm Springs assignment, and by now a working witch in everything but self-description. She has stopped being able to pretend that her magic is a favour to her teacher, and she has stopped being able to pretend that her order tells her the truth. She is still rigidly disciplined, still frightened of what she is becoming, and still living with the memory of turning Adrian down in the cruellest terms available to her.
characters.name: Sydney Sage

characters.description: A royal Moroi spirit user who was told, in the plainest possible language, that a relationship with him is unthinkable. He has not stopped feeling what he feels and has stopped bothering to hide it, which makes every conversation with Sydney an exercise in things neither of them will say. He can walk into other people's dreams, which is both useful and impossible to avoid.
characters.name: Adrian Ivashkov

characters.description: Sydney's history teacher and the witch training her, increasingly urgent about it. She has a sister she does not talk about and a reason for wanting Sydney strong enough to defend herself. Blunt, tired and fond of Sydney in a way she expresses mostly as homework.
characters.name: Jaclyn Terwilliger

characters.description: The Moroi queen's half-sister, still hidden at Amberwood and still the only thing keeping her sister on the throne. The bond with Adrian means she has lived through his heartbreak from the inside, and she knows exactly what Sydney did and why, which she cannot discuss with either of them.
characters.name: Jill Dragomir

characters.description: Jill's dhampir guardian, posing as her brother. Disciplined to a fault and now attached to Angeline, he continues to treat his own feelings as a professional failing.
characters.name: Eddie Castile

characters.description: The dhampir raised among the Keepers, still adjusting badly to human school and still solving problems with her fists. She is with Eddie now, and neither of them is entirely sure it is what they wanted.
characters.name: Angeline Dawes

characters.description: Sydney's lab partner, disowned by the Warriors of Light for helping her. He has lost the future his family planned for him and is working out what is left, while keeping the group's secrets.
characters.name: Trey Juarez

characters.description: Jaclyn Terwilliger's older sister and the reason for her urgency: a witch who takes the magic and the youth of younger witches, leaving them drained and comatose, and who grows stronger with every one she takes. An untrained witch of real power is precisely what she looks for.
characters.name: Veronica Terwilliger

characters.description: A Moroi spirit user and former Strigoi restored by spirit magic, now marrying after years apart from the man she loves. She is one of the few people who can see what Sydney's aura says about her, and she says it kindly.
characters.name: Sonya Karp

characters.description: A Moroi guardian who spent years searching for Sonya while she was Strigoi and who is now marrying her at the Moroi Court.
characters.name: Mikhail Tanner

characters.description: A dhampir guardian to the Moroi queen, blunt and famously reckless, and one of the very few people who has ever seen Sydney break the Alchemists' rules. Their history is the reason Sydney's order has never entirely trusted her.
characters.name: Rose Hathaway

characters.description: The one-eyed self-defence instructor whose lessons Sydney and Adrian keep returning to. His grasp of the world's stranger corners turns out to be better sourced than his manner suggests.
characters.name: Malachi Wolfe

characters.description: An Alchemist who left the order and survived it, now living off the books with a small group of former Alchemists who call themselves the Merry Men. He wears an indigo tattoo over his golden lily and claims to know what the order's tattoos really do to the people who wear them. Charismatic, evasive about his own plans, and very interested in recruiting Sydney.
characters.name: Marcus Finch

characters.description: Sydney's father, a career Alchemist whose marriage is collapsing and who intends to keep his youngest daughter and her career for himself. He regards Sydney's judgement as a liability and does not conceal it.
characters.name: Jared Sage

characters.description: A young witch on the edge of the local coven, apparently weak, apparently harmless and apparently very glad of the help offered to her.
characters.name: Alicia

characters.description: Sydney's younger sister, now committed to the Alchemists and hardened by the choice. She arrives in Palm Springs assigned to the same posting as Sydney, which makes her both family and a witness.
characters.name: Zoe Sage

recaps.ending: Veronica Terwilliger is not the last threat: Alicia, the harmless-seeming young witch on the coven's edge, has been draining witches herself and is the one who finally put Veronica beyond reach. She takes Sydney, intending to take her magic with her, and Sydney destroys her - using power she had spent a year refusing to admit she had, and afterwards being unable to unknow what she is. Sydney goes through with Marcus Finch's procedure and has the compulsion in her golden lily broken, so that she can lie to the Alchemists, refuse them and speak about them without the tattoo stopping her, while still appearing to be an obedient member of the order. She declines to run away with Marcus's group: she will stay inside and keep her people safe. Her family has broken apart in the divorce, and her younger sister Zoe has chosen their father and the Alchemists. Sydney finally admits what she feels and goes to Adrian; they become a couple, with the certainty that discovery would destroy them both. In the last pages Zoe arrives in Palm Springs as Sydney's new Alchemist partner, sent to live beside her and report on everything she does.
recaps.in_short: Sydney is hunting two things at once: Marcus Finch, the Alchemist who escaped the order, and a witch who steals the magic and youth of young witches. The witch is Veronica, Ms. Terwilliger's sister, and Sydney - untrained, powerful and unprotected - is exactly what she looks for. Marcus, found at last, shows Sydney what she half suspects: the golden lily tattoo carries compulsion that keeps Alchemists obedient and silent, and it can be broken. He wants her to run; she wants to stay and protect her people. Meanwhile the search for Veronica runs alongside a Court wedding, a collapsing family and a road trip with Adrian, whose feelings Sydney can no longer honestly deny. When Veronica is finally cornered she has already been drained by someone else: Alicia, a young witch everyone dismissed as harmless, who has been building her own power and now comes for Sydney's. Sydney destroys her with magic she can no longer pretend not to have. She has her tattoo broken, refuses to leave the Alchemists, and chooses Adrian - just as her sister Zoe arrives in Palm Springs to watch her.

recaps.text: Previously: Sydney Sage, an Alchemist, runs the Palm Springs assignment hiding Jill Dragomir, the Moroi queen's half-sister, whose death would cost the queen the throne. Jill attends Amberwood Prep as Sydney's sister, guarded by the dhampirs Eddie Castile and Angeline Dawes, while the royal Moroi Adrian Ivashkov, bonded to Jill since he healed her, lives nearby. Sydney has exposed one corrupt Alchemist, stopped a restored Strigoi who was murdering young Moroi women, and learned that human magic is real: her history teacher Jaclyn Terwilliger is a witch, and Sydney has an unusual gift she was raised to consider abominable. Her friend Trey Juarez turned out to have been raised among the Warriors of Light, a human society that considers every vampire an abomination; when the Warriors captured Sonya Karp - a Moroi who had been Strigoi and was restored - the group rescued her, at the cost of Trey's place among his own people. Afterwards Adrian told Sydney he loved her. She refused him in her order's language, that an Alchemist and a Moroi together is unthinkable, and it devastated him. She has also heard, for the first time, of an Alchemist named Marcus Finch who covered his golden lily with an indigo tattoo and walked away from the order.

Sydney and Adrian are keeping a careful distance that neither of them wants, made harder by his ability to reach her in dreams. Ms. Terwilliger's training turns urgent: young witches in the area are being found drained of their magic and their youth, left comatose, and the woman doing it is her own older sister Veronica. An untrained witch with real power is exactly what Veronica hunts, which makes Sydney a target and makes finishing her training a matter of survival rather than curiosity. At the same time Sydney has not let go of the name Clarence gave her - Marcus Finch, the Alchemist who covered his golden lily and disappeared - because if he got out, the order she has served all her life is not what it claims to be.

The group travels to the Moroi Court for the wedding of Sonya Karp and Mikhail Tanner, where Sydney moves among Moroi royalty as an Alchemist on duty and as a guest, and where she and Adrian spend an evening pretending nothing is happening between them. Court also gives Sydney access to Alchemist business and to people who knew Marcus Finch, and she comes away with a thread to pull. Back in Palm Springs, Ms. Terwilliger pushes her harder, Malachi Wolfe's odd expertise proves useful again, and Sydney begins working the kind of magic she used to insist she was only humouring her teacher by learning. Veronica claims another victim, and the search for her becomes a hunt with a schedule.

Sydney tracks Marcus Finch down. He is living outside the order with a handful of former Alchemists who call themselves the Merry Men, and he tells her what he learned before he ran: the golden lily on every Alchemist's cheek carries compulsion. It is not only a health charm and a seal on their tongues - it makes them loyal, keeps them from questioning orders, and can be reinforced. It can also be broken, by a painful procedure and a second tattoo, which is what the indigo lily over his own is. He wants Sydney to break hers and join him. Sydney, who has spent months noticing what her order does not tell her, believes him, and is not remotely willing to walk away from the people she is responsible for.

The hunt for Veronica takes Sydney and Adrian out on the road together, and the distance they have been keeping does not survive it. Sydney's family is coming apart at the same time: her parents' marriage ends, and Sydney does what she can to keep her younger sister Zoe away from their father and out of the Alchemists, which fails - Zoe chooses him, and holds Sydney's interference against her. Marcus's offer stays open while Sydney puts him off. A young witch called Alicia attaches herself to the coven's edge, apparently frightened and grateful for protection. Veronica's trail leads towards a confrontation Ms. Terwilliger has been dreading for most of her life, and Sydney is the strongest weapon either sister has.

When Sydney and Ms. Terwilliger finally close in on Veronica, they find her already destroyed - drained and left empty by a witch stronger than she was. None of the obvious candidates fit, and the answer, when it comes, is Alicia: the frightened, helpless young witch everyone dismissed, whose weakness was a pose and who has been quietly taking power from every witch who underestimated her. She is stronger now than Veronica ever was, and an untrained talent as large as Sydney's is the prize she has been circling from the start. Sydney has spent the whole hunt being frightened of the wrong woman, and the person who has been closest to her preparations is the one she should have been guarding against.

Alicia takes Sydney, intending to strip her magic the way she stripped Veronica's. What saves Sydney is the power she has spent a year refusing to claim: she uses it deliberately and at full strength, and Alicia does not survive it. Afterwards Sydney cannot unknow what she is. She goes to Marcus and has the compulsion in her golden lily broken: from now on she can lie to the Alchemists, refuse an order and speak about the order's business while still passing as a loyal member. She refuses to leave with the Merry Men - staying inside is how she protects Jill and the others - which makes her an Alchemist in appearance only, a far more dangerous position than defecting. Her family has split in the divorce, and Zoe has chosen their father and the order. And Sydney, having accepted what she is, finally admits what she wants: she goes to Adrian and tells him, and they begin a relationship that would destroy them both if it were discovered. In the last pages Zoe arrives in Palm Springs, assigned as Sydney's new Alchemist partner and housemate.

characters.description: Oberon's half-human daughter, sixteen and out of her depth. She is living in the Winter Court as Queen Mab's hostage, honouring the bargain she struck to get her brother back, cut off from her family, watched constantly, and safe only for as long as the queen finds her useful. Whatever passed between her and Ash on the road to Tir Na Nog, he now behaves as though it never happened.
characters.name: Meghan Chase

characters.description: The youngest son of Mab, the Winter prince who brought Meghan to Tir Na Nog under the terms of their bargain. Inside his mother's court he treats Meghan with public indifference sliding into open coldness, and he will not explain himself. What that performance costs him, if anything, is not something Meghan can see.
characters.name: Ash

characters.description: Queen of the Winter Court, ruling the Unseelie fey from Tir Na Nog. She holds Meghan under the terms of Ash's bargain and makes it clear that a Summer half-blood in her court exists on sufferance. She is elegant, absolute, and entirely uninterested in Meghan except as leverage against Oberon.
characters.name: Mab

characters.description: One of Mab's older sons, handsome and mocking, who takes obvious pleasure in Meghan's discomfort at court and in needling his youngest brother wherever it will do the most damage.
characters.name: Rowan

characters.description: Another of Mab's sons, older than Ash and steadier than Rowan. He is courteous to Meghan in a distant way and carries the duties of a Winter prince without the cruelty his brother brings to them.
characters.name: Sage

characters.description: The trickster who spent years disguised as Meghan's schoolfriend Robbie and then took her across the Nevernever to recover her brother. He serves Oberon, jokes his way through anything lethal, and his old feud with Ash has never been settled. Meghan left him behind when she went to Winter, and she does not know where he is.
characters.name: Puck

characters.description: The cait sith who guided Meghan through the Nevernever on her search for Ethan. He talks, vanishes at will, knows more than he says, and never gives anything away without agreeing a favour first, then collects it whenever it suits him.
characters.name: Grimalkin

characters.description: Meghan's young half brother, taken by the Iron fey and recovered from Machina's realm. He is home in Louisiana with their mother and stepfather, with no clear memory of where he was, and Meghan's family has no idea what she did to get him back.
characters.name: Ethan Chase

characters.description: The Erlking, ruler of the Summer Court and Meghan's father. He acknowledged her as his daughter but has never treated that as an obligation to protect her, and he did not intervene when she bargained herself away to Winter.
characters.name: Oberon

characters.description: The Exile Queen: a powerful fey thrown out of the Nevernever who now rules the exiles, half-breeds and strays living in the mortal world, from a mansion reached through the thorned wildland of the Briars. She keeps human musicians and artists in her house and feeds on their talent, deals in favours and information, and is generous in a way that always turns out to have terms attached.
characters.name: Leanansidhe

characters.description: A quiet pianist among the humans kept in Leanansidhe's mansion, known to the household as Charles. He has no memory of his own name or of how long he has been there. He is Paul Chase, Meghan's father, taken out of the mortal world on the day he disappeared eleven years ago.
characters.name: Paul Chase

characters.description: The huge black iron horse who once hunted Meghan across the Nevernever for Machina. With his king dead he comes to her not as an enemy but as a petitioner, holding that the Iron crown passed to Meghan when she destroyed Machina and that whoever wears it now is a usurper. He is loud, literal-minded and immovably loyal to a claim Meghan wants nothing to do with.
characters.name: Ironhorse

characters.description: An Iron fey serving the new claimant to the Iron throne, unhurried and precise, whose particular talent is infecting other fey with something that leaves them obedient and hollowed out. She treats the fey she takes as equipment rather than as enemies.
characters.name: Virus

recaps.ending: Meghan ends the war by walking onto the Reaping Fields between the assembled armies of Summer and Winter and returning the stolen Scepter of the Seasons, proving that Summer never took it and that the Iron fey both courts deny are real. She does it using iron glamour in front of Oberon and Mab, which saves a great many fey and simultaneously identifies her as the most dangerous creature on the field: a half-human princess who can wield the one power lethal to every full-blooded fey alive. Ironhorse does not survive. He gives his life destroying Virus and breaking the Iron fey's hold on the fight, serving Meghan as the queen he believed the Iron crown belonged to. Rowan is exposed as the traitor who sold Winter's secrets to the Iron fey and does not return to his mother's court. Ash has broken with Mab openly and stopped pretending to feel nothing. Oberon then banishes Meghan from the Nevernever, protection and precaution at the same time, and Ash is cast out of Winter for choosing her. The book closes with the two of them exiled together in the mortal world, the Iron fey still ruled by whoever took Machina's crown, and the Iron Realm still spreading into Faery with nobody willing to stop it.
recaps.in_short: Meghan Chase is living in the Winter Court as Mab's hostage, the price of the bargain that got her brother back, while Ash, the Winter prince she has fallen for, treats her with public contempt. When Iron fey ambush the ceremony that passes the Scepter of the Seasons between the courts, killing one of Mab's sons and stealing the Scepter, Winter blames Summer and declares war. Meghan escapes to the mortal world, finds Puck, and reaches Leanansidhe the Exile Queen, in whose mansion she discovers her long-missing human father, alive and stripped of his memory. Allied with Puck, Grimalkin, Ash and the Iron fey Ironhorse, who insists the Iron crown is hers by right, she steals the Scepter back, learns that Ash's brother Rowan has been the traitor feeding Winter's secrets to the Iron fey, and survives an attack on her own school in which Ironhorse sacrifices himself. Meghan returns the Scepter at the Reaping Fields and stops the war, but does it by wielding iron glamour in front of both courts. Oberon banishes her from the Nevernever, and Ash, who has chosen her over Winter, is exiled with her.

recaps.text: Previously: Meghan Chase learned on her sixteenth birthday that her four-year-old brother Ethan had been stolen and a changeling left in his place, and that her best friend Robbie was really Puck, the trickster, set to guard her by Oberon, Erlking of the Summer Court, who is her true father. Crossing into the Nevernever, she was acknowledged as Oberon's half-human daughter, made an enemy of his queen Titania, and struck a bargain with Ash, youngest son of Mab of the Winter Court: he would help her recover Ethan, and afterwards she would go with him to Winter as Mab's hostage. The kidnappers turned out to be the Iron fey, a new breed born of human faith in machines, whose iron kills traditional fey and whose existence both courts refuse to admit. Meghan destroyed their king, Machina, and freed Ethan, and Machina warned her as he died that the Iron fey would outlast him and that his crown would not stay empty. Meghan took her brother home, and Ash came to collect what she owed. She travelled with him to Tir Na Nog, and somewhere on that road whatever the two of them feel for each other stopped being deniable, which in Mab's court is the most dangerous thing either of them owns.

Meghan is living in the Winter Court as Mab's hostage under the terms of her bargain, a Summer half-blood at the heart of Winter, watched constantly and secure only while the queen finds her useful. Ash treats her with public indifference bordering on cruelty and offers no explanation. His brothers Rowan and Sage make their own use of her presence, Rowan by needling everyone within reach. The court is preparing for the exchange of the Scepter of the Seasons, the token that passes between Summer and Winter as the seasons turn and carries the power that holds them. The ceremony is ambushed. Iron fey attack, one of Mab's sons is killed, and the Scepter is taken. Mab, who will not admit the Iron fey are real, blames Summer for the theft and the death, and Winter goes to war.

With war declared and Meghan a Summer prisoner in a Winter court, staying is not survivable. Ash will not break with his mother where she can see it, and he denies outright everything that passed between them on the journey to Tir Na Nog; Meghan takes him at his word. She gets out of the Winter Court and back to the mortal world, discovering along the way how far the Iron fey's reach now extends and how little either court intends to do about it. What she has worked out is simple and unwelcome: the Scepter is in Iron hands, the two courts are about to destroy each other over a theft neither of them committed, and nobody with the power to stop it believes a word she says.

Back in the mortal world Meghan finds Puck again, and the two of them go looking for a way to reach the Iron fey. The road runs through the Briars, the thorned wildland between the worlds, and out the other side into the domain of Leanansidhe, the Exile Queen: a fey thrown out of the Nevernever who rules the exiles and half-breeds of the mortal world from a mansion full of human musicians and artists whose talent she feeds on. Leanansidhe trades in favours and information and is willing to help, at her own rates and on her own schedule. Among the humans kept in her house, Meghan notices a quiet pianist the household calls Charles.

The pianist is Paul Chase, Meghan's father, taken out of the mortal world on the day he vanished eleven years ago and left without a memory of his own name. She can neither restore him nor take him home. That leaves the Scepter. Ironhorse, once Machina's lieutenant and Meghan's pursuer, seeks her out as an ally rather than an enemy: with Machina dead he holds that the Iron crown became Meghan's when she destroyed him and that the one wearing it now is a usurper. Meghan, Puck, Grimalkin and Ironhorse move against the Iron fey to steal the Scepter back, and Ash finds his way to them. Inside, they meet Virus, an Iron fey who infects others with something that leaves them obedient and empty, and they learn who has been handing the Iron fey Winter's secrets. Rowan, Mab's own son, has been working with them from the start.

The Scepter is recovered, at a cost, and the fighting follows Meghan into the mortal world. Ash stops performing indifference and breaks with Winter openly rather than privately. Meghan comes out of the confrontation with the Iron fey badly hurt, and getting her healed costs her allies time the war does not leave them. What she discovers about herself is more dangerous than the injury: she can wield iron glamour, the power that kills every other fey in the Nevernever, and neither court will be able to see that as anything but a threat.

The Iron fey follow Meghan into her own life, attacking her school during the winter formal, and Ironhorse fights them there. When ending it means destroying Virus and the Iron fey's grip along with her, Ironhorse gives his own life to do it, dying in the service of the queen he chose. Meghan reaches the Reaping Fields, where the armies of Summer and Winter have met, and returns the Scepter of the Seasons in front of both courts, proving the theft was never Summer's doing and stopping the war before it begins. She does it by using iron glamour openly, in front of Oberon, Mab and everyone else present, which settles the argument about whether the Iron fey exist and makes Meghan herself the thing the courts are now most afraid of. Rowan's treachery is exposed and he does not come back. Oberon banishes his daughter from the Nevernever, and Ash, who has already chosen her over Winter, is cast out too. The book closes with Meghan home in the mortal world, exiled from Faery, with Ash beside her.

characters.description: A girl turning sixteen in rural Louisiana, living on her stepfather's hog farm with her mother and her four-year-old half brother Ethan. Her own father walked out of her life when she was six and was never found. Poor, unpopular and largely invisible at school, she is stubborn and fiercely protective of Ethan, and she has spent years quietly ignoring the things she keeps seeing at the edge of her vision.
characters.name: Meghan Chase

characters.description: Meghan's four-year-old half brother, attached to a stuffed rabbit and to Meghan herself. He insists that a man hides in his bedroom closet and that things move through the house at night, claims the adults around him dismiss.
characters.name: Ethan Chase

characters.description: Meghan's mother, who married Luke Chase and built a quiet life on his farm. She is protective in a way Meghan finds stifling, and she deflects every question about Meghan's father and about the years before her second marriage.
characters.name: Melissa Chase

characters.description: Meghan's biological father, who disappeared when she was six: he took her out for the day, walked away toward the water, and was never seen again. No trace of him was ever found, and the unexplained loss shaped the family Meghan grew up in.
characters.name: Paul Chase

characters.description: Meghan's best friend at school, a red-haired troublemaker she has known for years as Robbie Goodfell. When the truth about Ethan comes out he stops pretending: he is Robin Goodfellow, the trickster called Puck, and he has been posing as a schoolboy in order to keep watch over Meghan on the orders of a master in the fey world whose name he will not give her. He treats mortal danger as entertainment and jokes without pause, but he is a very old and very capable creature underneath it.
characters.name: Puck

characters.description: A grey cat of the Nevernever, a cait sith, who talks, vanishes at will and appears to know a great deal about everyone he meets. He agrees to guide Meghan on the strict understanding that she will owe him a favour to be named at a time of his choosing. He gives excellent advice, refuses to fight, and leaves whenever a situation stops being interesting.
characters.name: Grimalkin

characters.description: Ruler of the Summer Court of the Nevernever and, as Meghan learns, her true father. Ancient, formal and difficult to read, he acknowledges her openly as his half-human daughter and admits that he placed Puck at her side years ago. His evident care for her sits uneasily beside his refusal to send the Summer Court after whatever took her brother.
characters.name: Oberon

characters.description: Queen of the Summer Court and Oberon's wife, radiant, imperious and quick to anger. Meghan's existence is public proof of her husband's affair with a mortal woman, and Titania makes no secret of wanting the girl out of her court by whatever means the rules of Faery allow.
characters.name: Titania

characters.description: The youngest son of Mab, Queen of the Winter Court, a prince who hunts for his mother and has a reputation for never coming back empty-handed. He is cold, exact and courteous, and Oberon's half-human daughter is exactly the sort of prize his queen would want. Under the truce that governs the courts' shared gatherings he cannot simply take her, which leaves bargaining, and he is very patient.
characters.name: Ash

characters.description: Queen of the Winter Court, Titania's opposite and equal, who rules the Unseelie fey from Tir Na Nog. She is Ash's mother, and her interest in Oberon's half-human daughter is not a friendly one.
characters.name: Mab

characters.description: The Iron King: ruler of a new kind of fey, and the figure Meghan glimpsed moving inside her computer screen and Ethan saw standing in his closet. His creatures took Ethan, and everywhere his realm spreads the old fey sicken, rust and die.
characters.name: Machina

characters.description: A fey seer hiding in New Orleans in the shape of an old woman, who trades in knowledge of what is coming. She knows what took Meghan's brother and where it lives, and she will say so only at a price she sets herself.
characters.name: The Oracle

characters.description: One of the Iron King's lieutenants, an enormous horse built of black iron and steam who leads the hunt for Meghan and her companions. He is relentless, deafening, and oddly formal about the duty he owes his king.
characters.name: Ironhorse

recaps.ending: Meghan destroys Machina in his own tower and frees Ethan from the machinery that was keeping the Iron King alive, but Machina's last words are a warning rather than a plea: the Iron fey exist because humans believe in machines, that belief is not going away, and his crown will find another head. Ash, who held off the Iron knights so that Meghan could reach the tower, survives; Puck and Grimalkin come through as well, and Grimalkin's favour is still unclaimed. Meghan gets Ethan back to Louisiana and to a family who will never know where he was. The Summer Court has acknowledged her without protecting her, Titania remains an enemy, and both courts still refuse to admit the Iron fey are real, which leaves the underlying problem entirely unsolved. Then Meghan's own bargain comes due: Ash arrives at her house to take her to Tir Na Nog, where she will be Mab's hostage as agreed. She goes willingly. The next book opens with her inside the Winter Court, in the hands of a queen with no reason to be kind to Oberon's daughter, beside a prince whose feelings for her are a danger to them both.
recaps.in_short: Meghan Chase turns sixteen in rural Louisiana and comes home to find her four-year-old brother Ethan replaced by a hostile changeling. Her best friend Robbie admits he is really Puck, the trickster, set to watch over her by Oberon, king of the Summer Court, who is Meghan's true father. Crossing into the fey world to get Ethan back, Meghan is acknowledged as a half-blood princess of Summer, loathed by Queen Titania, and forced to bargain with Ash, the Winter Court prince sent to catch her: he will help her, and afterwards she belongs to his mother, Mab. The search leads to a new kind of fey born from human faith in technology, whose iron is lethal to the old courts and whose existence Faery refuses to acknowledge. Their king, Machina, took Ethan to draw Meghan in. In his dying realm he offers her a place at his side; she refuses and destroys him, freeing her brother, while Machina promises that the Iron fey and their empty throne will outlast him. Meghan takes Ethan home, then leaves with Ash to pay what she owes.

recaps.text: Meghan Chase turns sixteen on a hog farm in rural Louisiana, where she lives with her mother, her stepfather Luke and her four-year-old half brother Ethan. Her own father walked away when she was six and was never found. Around her birthday the strangeness she has spent years ignoring stops being ignorable: Ethan insists a man hides in his closet, something moves inside her computer screen, and her best friend Robbie Goodfell begins behaving as though he is expecting trouble. After a humiliating day at school Meghan comes home to find Ethan changed, vicious and wrong and no longer her brother. Robbie tells her what she is looking at: the real Ethan has been taken into the fey world and a changeling left in his place. Then he drops the disguise he has worn for years.
